nodes.label: MADRAG: Multi-Agent Debate with Retrieval-Augmented Generation
nodes.rationale: Training-free framework for analytic essay scoring combining multi-agent debate (Advocate, Skeptic, Judge) with retrieval-augmented exemplar grounding.

nodes.label: Advocate Agent
nodes.rationale: Specialized agent role highlighting essay strengths without assigning scores or discussing weaknesses; provides opening argument emphasizing positive aspects.

nodes.label: Skeptic Agent
nodes.rationale: Specialized agent role critiquing essay weaknesses without assigning scores or mentioning strengths; produces rebuttal focused on shortcomings.

nodes.label: Judge Agent
nodes.rationale: Impartial arbiter synthesizing Advocate and Skeptic arguments with confidence scores and retrieved exemplars to produce final integer score.

nodes.label: ASAP Dataset
nodes.rationale: Widely used benchmark of student-written English essays scored by trained raters using prompt-specific rubrics; includes eight essay sets with trait-level annotations for Sets 7 and 8.

nodes.label: Quadratic Weighted Kappa (QWK)
nodes.rationale: Standard agreement metric in AES accounting for ordinal score distances; used to evaluate trait-level scoring performance.

nodes.label: ProTACT
nodes.rationale: Supervised neural model for analytic trait scoring introducing prompt-aware representations and trait-similarity objective (Do et al., 2023).

nodes.label: Middle-Score Bias
nodes.rationale: Systematic bias in LLM-as-judge where models cluster predictions toward center of scoring scale, avoiding extreme values even when warranted (Zheng et al., 2023).

nodes.label: MADRAG: Multi-Agent Debate with Retrieval-Augmented Generation
nodes.rationale: Multi-agent debate framework combining adversarial reasoning (Advocate-Skeptic) with retrieval-augmented exemplar grounding for essay trait scoring; designed to improve calibration and reduce systematic biases in LLM-based assessment.

nodes.label: ASAP Essay Dataset
nodes.rationale: Benchmark dataset with 8 essay sets; Sets 7 and 8 selected for trait-level evaluation due to availability of independent multi-rater scores per essay, enabling study of human-human agreement and model calibration under rater disagreement.

nodes.label: Advocate-Skeptic Debate Protocol
nodes.rationale: Single-round debate structure where Advocate presents evidence-heavy pro argument followed by Skeptic rebuttal; empirically more stable than multi-round debates and skeptic-first ordering, reducing verbosity and drift while preserving coverage of both strengths and weaknesses.

nodes.label: Token Myopia Failure Mechanism
nodes.rationale: Systematic error where MADRAG treats anonymization markers (@CAPS, @PERSON, @DATE) as genuine mechanical errors, leading to under-scoring on Conventions trait; occurs when surface-form noise is amplified by debate and retrieval interaction.

nodes.label: Debate Capture Failure Mechanism
nodes.rationale: Judge inherits Advocate/Skeptic framing without verifying claims against essay text; substitutes debate resolution for text verification, producing overconfident misdiagnoses about structure and coherence despite clear textual evidence.

nodes.label: Rubric-Template Collapse Failure Mechanism
nodes.rationale: Under uncertainty, MADRAG falls back on plausible-sounding rubric prose weakly tied to essay content; reduces sensitivity to extremes and enables large deviations when essay is clearly strong or weak, indicating baseline judge limitation rather than component-specific artifact.

nodes.label: Analytic Essay Trait Scoring Task
nodes.rationale: Multi-trait assessment of student essays on dimensions like Ideas, Organization, Style, Conventions; requires understanding of rubric-aligned criteria, synthesis of evidence, and calibration under rater disagreement; tests both reasoning quality and reliability.
